title: Hitwicket 200 million users: Metasports' cricket bet
description: Hitwicket 200 million users is the goal Kashyap Reddy sets as Metasports pushes cricket gaming globally, according to MediaNews4U. Here is what we know.

body.text: Hitwicket 200 million users is the ambition Kashyap Reddy puts on the table, according to a MediaNews4U report, as Metasports bets on cricket gaming going global. For Indian players, it is a sign that a cricket-first mobile game is being pitched as a worldwide product, not only a domestic one. It also shows how seriously builders are taking cricket as a gaming category.
The headline carries the main claims. Hitwicket is aiming for 200 million users, and Metasports is making a bet on global cricket gaming. Reddy is the person quoted in the title.

We should be clear about the limits here. The text we had access to is mostly a set of unrelated snippets from the MediaNews4U page, so we cannot confirm the full interview. We do not have a timeline for the target, the current user count, revenue figures or specific product plans. Treat the 200 million figure as a stated goal, not a result.
What Hitwicket 200 million users would mean

A target of that size puts Hitwicket in a very different league from a niche sports title. Reaching it would almost certainly depend on audiences outside India, which fits the global framing in the headline. Cricket's following in many countries is the obvious logic behind the plan, though the report as we have it does not lay out that reasoning.

For Indian gamers, the interesting part is that cricket games are being built with a global audience in mind from the start. That could shape features, languages and competitive formats over time, but none of that is confirmed in the material we saw.

The same MediaNews4U page carries a separate item saying India's gaming market is expected to nearly double, from $5.02 billion in 2026 to $9.89 billion by 2031. That snippet is cut off after mentioning mobile, so we cannot say what drives the forecast. It is also not linked to Hitwicket in the text we have. Still, it gives context for why a cricket gaming company would talk big about scale.

items: Whether Hitwicket or Metasports shares a timeline for the 200 million user goal.
Any disclosure of the current user base, so the target can be judged against a starting point.
Signs of expansion into new countries or cricket formats.
Whether the game's competitive and community features grow alongside the user push.

body.text: Until more detail comes out, the 200 million figure is an ambition worth tracking, not a milestone. We will update this story if the full interview or a company statement adds specifics.

faqs.a: According to MediaNews4U's headline, Hitwicket is targeting 200 million users. The part of the report available to us does not spell out a timeline or how that number would be counted.

faqs.q: Who is Kashyap Reddy in this story?
faqs.a: MediaNews4U names Kashyap Reddy in its headline as the voice behind the 200 million user target and the global cricket gaming bet. The material we reviewed does not describe his role in detail.

faqs.q: How big is India's gaming market expected to get?
faqs.a: A separate item shown on the MediaNews4U page says India's gaming market is expected to nearly double from $5.02 billion in 2026 to $9.89 billion by 2031. That figure is not part of the Hitwicket interview itself.
